description: Color harmony as circular algebra — the mathematical formalism underlying all classical harmony systems, extended with generative variants

circle_model.domain: S¹ — the unit circle, parameterized by angle θ ∈ [0°, 360°)
circle_model.mapping: HSL hue H maps directly to angle θ. The color wheel IS the circle.
circle_model.arithmetic: All harmony operations are addition mod 360

harmony_as_symmetry.description: Each harmony type corresponds to a symmetry group acting on the circle
harmony_as_symmetry.generalization: An n-adic harmony is generated by a rotation of 360/n degrees. The hue angles form a regular n-gon inscribed in the color wheel.

operations.reflect_axis: θ' = (2α - θ) mod 360  [reflection across axis at angle α]

distance_metrics.notes: Circular distance is symmetric and bounded by 180°. Two colors are 'maximally different' in hue when d = 180° (complementary).

harmonies.name: Monochromatic
harmonies.description: Single hue, multiple values. Unified and serene.
harmonies.generative_tip: Map a 1D noise or LFO to S and L while holding H fixed. Use sine functions at different frequencies for S and L for organic variation.
harmonies.art_notes: Monochromatic is restraint as a choice. One hue controls everything; the drama comes from value contrast. Works beautifully in generative systems where you want texture without color chaos.

harmonies.name: Analogous
harmonies.description: Neighboring hues. Natural, harmonious, found in nature. Low tension.
harmonies.generative_tip: Use analogous for background/ambient color fields, then punch with a complementary accent. The 30° spread is the minimum — try ±15° for extra cohesion, ±45° for more variety.
harmonies.art_notes: Nature runs on analogous palettes: sunsets, foliage, ocean water. They read as belonging together without analysis. Use when you want beauty without confrontation.

harmonies.name: Analogous Wide
harmonies.description: Five neighboring hues. More variation, still cohesive.
harmonies.generative_tip: Assign each of the 5 hues a different role: background, midground, foreground, accent, highlight. The 120° total span gives enough contrast to read as distinct while staying harmonious.
harmonies.art_notes: Wide analogous is the workhorse of complex generative systems. Wide enough to feel varied, narrow enough to feel intentional. Five slots maps naturally to layered renders.

harmonies.name: Split Complementary
harmonies.description: Primary + two colors adjacent to its complement. High contrast, less tension than direct complementary.
harmonies.generative_tip: Use the base hue for the dominant mass, the two split complements as accents at different opacities. The asymmetry (150° vs 210°) creates directional tension.
harmonies.art_notes: Split complementary is the diplomatic complement — it gives you most of the contrast energy of a complementary pair but with an escape route. More sophisticated than straight complementary, less aggressive.

harmonies.name: Triadic
harmonies.description: Three equally spaced hues. Vibrant and balanced. The primary color triad (red/yellow/blue) is triadic.
harmonies.generative_tip: Rotate θ slowly over time (0.5°/frame) for animated palette cycling. Use one color at 60% presence, others at 20% each — triadic breaks down when all three fight for dominance.
harmonies.art_notes: Triadic is the equilateral triangle — maximally fair, maximally energetic. The classic primaries (red/yellow/blue) are triadic. Nothing is allowed to be quiet.

harmonies.name: Square / Tetradic
harmonies.description: Four equally spaced hues. Rich and complex. Hard to balance — vary saturation/lightness heavily.
harmonies.generative_tip: Desaturate two of the four colors heavily. A square palette with 4 equally saturated colors is overwhelming — balance requires giving two colors a supporting role.
harmonies.art_notes: Square tetradic is the most structurally complete harmony and the hardest to use well. Four maximally spread hues means every warm-cool pair is present simultaneously. Requires compositional discipline.

harmonies.name: Rectangular / Double Complementary
harmonies.description: Two complementary pairs. Rectangle on the wheel.
harmonies.generative_tip: Think of it as two complementary relationships. Use each pair in separate spatial zones — they'll reinforce each other's contrast without fighting for the same territory.
harmonies.art_notes: Rectangular tetradic gives you two independent complementary tensions. The 60° gap makes one pair 'warm dominant' and one 'cool dominant'. Sophisticated and a bit dangerous.

harmonies.name: Complementary
harmonies.description: Two hues opposite on the wheel. Maximum contrast. Can vibrate visually at equal weight.
harmonies.generative_tip: Use one color at 70% area, complement at 30% for balance. At 50/50 equal chroma and lightness they will vibrate — use that intentionally or avoid it by adjusting L.
harmonies.art_notes: Complementary is the nuclear option. Maximum hue distance, maximum vibration potential. This is the palette of warning signs and sports teams for a reason.

golden_angle.irrationality: 137.508° / 360° is irrational (= 2 - φ). No two golden-angle steps land on the same hue modulo 360°.
golden_angle.density: The sequence {n × 137.508° mod 360° : n ∈ ℕ} is equidistributed on [0°, 360°) — guaranteed by the three-distance theorem.
golden_angle.generative_tip: Step through golden angle hues for automatic maximum-spread palettes of any size. Works for n=2 through n=∞. No two consecutive colors are ever near each other.
golden_angle.art_notes: The golden angle is nature's solution to packing maximum distinct items on a circle. Sunflower seeds, leaf spirals, pinecone scales. Use it when you need n distinct colors and don't want to think about it.

fibonacci_ratio.name: Fibonacci Ratio Harmony
fibonacci_ratio.convergence: Ratios converge to 1/φ ≈ 0.618, which maps to the golden angle
fibonacci_ratio.generative_tip: Generate palettes where early steps cluster (0.5 = complementary, 0.667 = triadic) and later steps approach golden angle spread. Interesting for temporal animations that start with familiar harmony.
fibonacci_ratio.art_notes: Fibonacci harmony starts familiar and gets stranger. The first two steps give you complementary then triadic; by step 10 you're essentially at golden angle. Animate through this sequence for palettes that feel like they're discovering themselves.

prime_gap.name: Prime Gap Harmony
prime_gap.generative_tip: Scale factor 30 maps single-gap to 30°, creating analogous-to-triadic range. Scale 50 makes twin primes (gap=2) into 100° jumps. Twin prime clusters create palette runs that look almost analogous, then suddenly jump far.
prime_gap.art_notes: Prime gap palettes are the most interesting irregular sequence for color. They're not random — they're deterministic — but they feel non-systematic. The twin prime clusters create local cohesion; large gaps (prime deserts) create drama.

tension_algebra.description: Perceptual tension between two hue angles, normalized to [0, 1]
